In all six, calendars_from_now pressed Return on Date's Calendars while that row still read Calendars with an ellipsis, asking, just after timekeeping.socket started again, and that row's Return only closed, so the launcher closed under Joel's way to the calendars. It comes off once twenty net runs in a row after the fix exit 0, counted by exit code, since a failure only here is recorded as passed: at 6 in 39, twenty pass by luck about one time in thirty. A launcher closed at that Return means the fix is wrong. A wait for the four calendars that runs out, its 60 s covering the reader's start, means the fix is wrong if the journal says 'calendars held' at any point after the socket started again while the step still holds no rows, and a slow or hung reader if it doesn't; back at Date means the reader refused. Only a closed launcher and an answer that never filled the step count against the fix; any other failure restarts the count. If twenty in a row haven't passed by the end of 24 Nov UTC, its owner moves the due and sends the new one before this one passes. While it stands, nothing catches a change that breaks what the subtest checks: Date's calendars with the reader gone and back, the clock's figures, chrony's servers and their drawers, Time with chronyd stopped, and Time keeping one Clock when its reader answers late

Its owner, the call shaper's, read on 23 Nov where the calls' datagrams went in the net's runs that lost past the bar, and the fix that answers what was the builder's (#6406, declaring the rig's line at its slowest busy hour) lands by 25 Nov 18:00 EST. With the shaper stopped on 20 Nov (00ddeee71091), the client's own receive buffers overflowed, 376 datagrams, iperf3 starved on the builder: the calls' sockets now have room for seconds of datagrams, and the bar counts only what was lost before the client's socket. Shaped in that run, the shaper's IFB dropped them, media's 12 all in its video tin and the page call's beside the app's downloads in best effort; and on 20 Nov (f0197badd1be) the router's down queue dropped 441 of the media call while nothing limited the download. The router's are the download hold's to prevent (jitsusama/shaper-holds-the-download-for-a-call): while a call is on and the download carries nine tenths of its declared 75 Mbit/s, under the router's 90, or the controller cuts it, the shaper holds it there, so it queues in the IFB's CAKE, where the call goes first, and that fix moved the due from 2026-11-27. A handshake reply lost coming down failed a call on 22 Nov (519b71b08ac0) with a stale errno, and is now made again as any lost handshake is, but only while the shaper's IFB dropped nothing meanwhile in the video and voice tins a call comes down in, so one lost while the shaper's own call tins dropped still fails. Every machine on a call's path now counts its datagrams each way, printed on a pass too, and a count under what iperf3 read fails, so a counter that misses the call can't read as nothing lost. test_a_call_loses_little bars a hundredth of a call lost coming down before the client's socket, and test_a_call_goes_ahead_of_its_own_uploads a hundredth of it dropped by the shaper's video tin going up. Its due is when it comes off, three days after the fix lands, since twenty runs after the fix take about two and a quarter at the net's pace of about nine a day. That leaves room for about seven runs more, so a red run past the seventh run after the fix, which starts the count again, moves the due, and its owner sends the new one before this one passes. It comes off once twenty net runs in a row after the fix exit 0, counted by exit code, since a failure only here is recorded as passed: at 4 in 26, three pass by luck about three times in five, and twenty about once in thirty. Before: the net excused 7 failures from 14 to 18 Nov, and about 5 in 20 runs failed after its failure trace was added, each a call losing 69 to 3,106 datagrams down, once with the shaper stopped, or the shaper not holding within 60 s, which #5897's asking a dark network again soon answered: none of the 15 net runs since it failed so. test_a_call_goes_ahead_of_its_own_uploads joined it on 20 Nov for sharing that holding wait and the call's bars, not for a failure of its own, and while it is listed a failure in it alone is said and blocks nothing, before a merge or after, so until it comes off nothing catches a change that stops telling Joel's CAKE its rate: the unit tests cover only the rate chosen and the command's form

Its owner, the shaper's, found the cause on 23 Nov and fixes it by 2026-11-25 18:00 EST, three days before its due, when it comes off. The test's client ran on one core: at b18b11bc945b its CAKE sent under the shaper's limit with data waiting and its kernel said htb had too many events, so the shaper, reading the client's own sending as the line's, cut again a second after its first cut, to 5391, and learned a plateau of 5280 to hold under, a median of 5016. The shaper climbs only while the client carries three quarters of its limit, so a client that falls behind drifts toward such a plateau instead, which is how the halved rate stayed low after the link came back. Neither is the shaper's on a real line: the owner's record of 22 Nov holds 1,312 cuts, and none of the 11 that came within 3 s of the one before stacked downward. The fix gives the client a second core, and a passing run prints its median, each reading's rate beside what the link's queues sent and held waiting, naming a client that fell behind, and the climb, from what rate and how long. It comes off once twenty net runs in a row after the fix exit 0 and their printed medians, readings and climbs show no client falling behind: at the 8 in 61 rate of 16 to 19 Nov ten pass by luck one time in four, but at the one failure in 30 seen since, twenty pass by luck about half the time, so the count alone can't show a fix. A red run past the seventh run after the fix, which starts the count again, moves the due. 8 of 61 net runs from 16 to 19 Nov exited 1, and each of the six whose logs remain held the upload under 6000, three failing here at medians of 5754 to 5887 and three timing out in a fixture, once never finding the connection in 90 s, at 4158, and twice never climbing back past 6000 from the halved rate in 120 s, once reaching 4880, as one failing here did too, still at 3923. While it stands, a run whose failed subtests are all listed, any of this one and the entry below's two, is excused whole, the net naming a subtest whose fixture timed out as failed, and so is one that loses its machine after them, its later lines dropped, but one cut off at its time limit names no subtest and is excused by nothing; a timeout in loaded names all six and isn't excused. Every other check in this subtest goes unguarded, among them its 8800 ceiling, answered pings, 80 ms ping bound, pings ending within 60 s and the shaper's status file being there
reason: failed on main at 89dc01f5ad2a twice, 3c36b575e846, 38063460e6a0, e3932cb77356 twice and 7030d16c46ae twice, passing between; #5615, the Mycelium lock where the net last met it, didn't cause it

due_why: Its owner, the margin cat's, takes it off once twenty net runs in a row exit 0 after the fix for its cause merges. It failed at a6901f968d03 and on a loaded lender at 847f070456cd the same way: the cat drew 8 frames of its own under the launcher, {'cat winit': 8, 'launcher': 8}, while its still neighbours drew none. The cause, found on 23 Nov: Joel's shell unit sets QT_WAYLAND_FRAME_CALLBACK_TIMEOUT=0, but the nested-niri checks ran the shell on Qt's 100 ms default, so a loaded builder's late frame callbacks had Qt take the cat's window for hidden and draw it again as each came. With the timeout set to 5 ms, an idle lender failed this case the same way, 17 frames, and two other frame-count cases with it. The fix has every check built by shellOnNiri read the setting from the unit, and has the cat follow every frame of a walk rather than ask of frames one by one, which drew a frame with each ask; the two landed together, so which of them ended the held walk's frames isn't told apart. The net runs this check at most heads that move the shell, 20 to 55 times a day from 18 to 22 Nov. The closed row's failures, 3 in 66 runs and not yet read, end the same run of twenty, so twenty in a row take about 34 runs, one to two days while main moves. While it stands, nothing catches the cat drawing or stepping under the launcher, or its walk not going on from where it was held. Its owner moves the due and says why before this date if a run fails

That holds only where the ride began, since the cat says how far its ground is off; a way across is held only where it sets off, and each later place on the ride is held to the way it was laid and its ground to never being carried farther off, which assumes the theme's spring never overshoots, and how far its ground is off is proven frame by frame in Qt's engine. The closed row's failures are not yet read; the frame callback timeout the entry above names may bear on them, which is untested. The closed row's case failed on main at 0e420d94fa78 twice and f76d551d20c1, its way off beginning turns, lands rather than rides, lands, shakes, and once hanging 1.16 s, passing between, in 3 of the net's 66 runs of the check from 20 to 22 Nov; the fourth failing run of either case, at 1e68b60f40fe, was the second move's alone. At 3 in 66 twenty pass by luck about two times in five, so the count alone can't show its fix: the fix also names the cause it found, as one of those failing runs' logs shows it, and keeps what the case asserts. While it stands, nothing here catches a closed row's fall hanging, being shoved or not landing on the window left, or a second move putting the cat where it never got to or not moving it on; MarginCatFalls.js's cases in Qt's engine still prove the fall frame by frame
